accepted_taxonomy.source: Kew Plants of the World Online
accepted_taxonomy.infraspecific_note: The widespread Texas taxon is commonly treated as var. curtipendula; the learner remains at species level unless a specimen is keyed to variety.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common Central Texas prairie grass with unusually obvious inflorescence architecture and several useful local Bouteloua comparisons.

target_zone_range.evidence_note: BONAP maps the species as native in Texas; USDA PLANTS-derived county data for var. curtipendula documents numerous project target-zone counties. Texas Hill Country herbarium vouchers independently include Blanco, Burnet, Comal, Kimble, and Williamson.

look_here_first: Go straight to the seed stalk. Numerous short lateral branches sit along the main axis and the spikelets hang to one side like tiny oats. Even old stalks often retain the one-sided branch attachment pattern.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Perennial bunchgrass; seed stalk bears many short lateral branches with several spikelets arranged to one side; vegetatively, look for a tiny membranous ligule and occasional papilla-based hairs near the blade/collar base.

morphology_keys.habit: Cespitose bunchgrass, usually 50–100 cm tall in the Texas Hill Country; short rhizomes may be present, stolons absent.
morphology_keys.sheaths: Rounded; generally open; glabrous to hirsute externally.
morphology_keys.collar: Continuous and mostly glabrous; margins may have a few papilla-based hairs.
morphology_keys.ligule: Very short (<0.5 mm), membranous, truncate, with erose/ciliate margin.
morphology_keys.leaf_blades: Linear, about 2–7 mm wide; usually flat and firm; some papilla-based hairs can occur near the base/margins.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Many short lateral raceme-like branches along an elongate rachis; several spikelets are borne on one side of each branch, producing the classic 'side-oats' look.
best_field_traits: many short lateral branches down the flowering axis
spikelets concentrated on one side of each branch
2–7 mm blades with occasional papilla-based basal hairs

lookalikes.separator: Usually shorter (about 15–40 cm) with much narrower 1–2 mm blades and distinctly pilose collar margins. Sideoats grama is taller with broader blades and the conspicuous many-branched side-oats inflorescence.
Texas grama has a ligule that is primarily a fringe of hairs and narrower 1–2 mm blades; sideoats grama has a minute membranous ligule and typically broader 2–7 mm blades.

diagnostic_image_roles: short lateral branch and spikelet arrangement
leaf base / collar / ligule when available

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prioritize views that make the one-sided lateral spikelets obvious, then add habit and leaf-base structure.

ecology.habitat: Grasslands, prairie, woodland borders/openings, rocky limestone slopes, and roadsides.
ecology.season: Warm-season; flowers/sets seed mainly summer into fall in Central Texas.
